messages:
Anna: heads-up — saw a perf regression on the fp8+int8 path after switching the default calibration to per-channel. p99 up ~12% on long-seq workloads, and kernel selector is flipping to the multi-pass fallback on some batches.
Kevin: can you paste the repro & perf output?
Anna: repro is a small bench we run on prod-like traces. snippet from the profiler:
```
KernelSelection: chosen=quant_multi_pass (fallback)
Reason: scale_variance>threshold (per-channel)
BatchStats: seq_len_avg=384 seq_len_p95=1024 batch_size=8
KVCache: miss_ratio=0.18 cache_evictions=23
Latency(p99): baseline=48ms -> current=54ms
```
Ryan: interesting — KV miss ratio of 18% is high for those traces. that plus seq tails could push selector into the slower path.
Sarah: what did the calibration set look like? long examples can blow per-channel ranges if they contain rare tokens.
Anna: exact issue: our calibration set had ~200 samples but skewed to long developer-chat logs and stacktraces. per-channel scales for some outlier channels exploded, which made quant kernels choose the conservative path.
Kevin: so the calibration procedure amplified outliers. did you use per-channel min/max or percentile clipping?
Anna: min/max with small epsilon. no percentile clipping. also used full-range hist-based scale which is noisy on small sample count.
Maria: quick thought — for runtime, two levers: (1) change calibration to per-tensor with 99th percentile clipping, (2) keep per-channel but clamp scales to a global multiplier to avoid huge ratios. tradeoffs: per-tensor reduces accuracy on some layers but avoids kernel fallback.
Ryan: also worth checking batching heuristics: if a few long seqs slip into an otherwise short batch, the selector might pick a different kernel early. maybe we should bias the selector to consider batch tail distribution rather than only p95.
Kevin: agree. we can add a quick heuristic: if seq_len_p95/seq_len_median > 3 then prefer fast single-pass if cumulative token cost delta < X.
Sarah: on calibration dataset selection — we should remove rare-token heavy samples or downweight them. propose: build calibration corpus from uniform sampling across request types with cap on length and a separate held-out long form set for tail-specific autoscaling.
Anna: I'm going to run two experiments:
- exp-A: per-tensor symmetric quant + 99th percentile clip (calib set trimmed)
- exp-B: per-channel but clamp scales to max_ratio=8 and apply per-channel 95th percentile clipping
Both will include kernel decision and KV hit logging.
perf-bot: CI regression alert: +11.8% p99 on integration/job/long-seq-bench with current main (regression window 12h).
devops-bot: rolling trace capture enabled for trace-id 0x7f3c; logs will be forwarded to /tmp/quant-traces/2412345678.tar.gz
Maria: config to enable debug logs (use locally on canary):
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DEBUG="kernel,kv,quant_calib"
./bin/serve --canary --trace=2412345678
```
Kevin: please also enable `RW_LOG_LEVEL=debug` for selector module and capture a few samples.
Anna: running exp-A now; will post numbers. exp-B queued after. target: 24h runs with p50/p95/p99 and kernel_choice distribution.
Sarah: I'll prepare a cleaned calib sampler script to avoid rare tokens and cap lengths. command I'll use: `python tools/calib_sampler.py --seed 42 --max-samples 1000 --max-length 512 --exclude-tags stacktrace,code`
Maria: also add logging for kv cache hit rate per-request: `metrics.kv_hit_rate` exported to prometheus.
perf-bot: update — first exp run (exp-A) halfway: p99 delta down to +2.1% vs baseline. kernel fallback rate reduced by ~70%.
Anna: promising. if exp-A keeps things within 3% we'll prefer per-tensor+clip as a short-term fix. exp-B still needed for layerwise accuracy testing.
Kevin: action items:
- Anna: finish exp-A & exp-B and post results (24h)
- Sarah: push calib sampler and share sample set hash
- Maria: enable selector/kv debug in canary and add prometheus kv hit metric
- Ryan: draft selector heuristic for batch-tail handling (PR)
Anna: noted. will update thread with final numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
